chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Al-Hasan, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Umar, from his brother Al-Husayn, from his father Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and with him was a man. The man said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I love the children.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'So what do you do?' He said, 'I carry them on my back.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) placed his hand on his forehead and turned his face away from him. The man wept, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at him as if he pitied him, and said, 'When you go to your city, buy a fat camel, tie it with a strong rope, take the sword and strike the hump with a strike that peels off its skin, and sit upon it while it is warm.'

Umar said, 'The man said, 'I went to my city and bought a camel, tied it with a strong rope, took the sword and struck the hump with it, peeled off its skin, and sat upon it while it was warm. Something resembling a lizard, smaller than a lizard, dropped from me onto the back of the camel, and what was in me settled down.'

key_terms.سَكَنَ مَا بِي: What was in me settled down

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Imam's instruction to strike the camel's hump and sit on it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds to a man’s declaration of love for children by instructing him to sit on a camel’s warm hump after peeling its skin, causing a 'lizard-like' creature to fall from him. Shia scholars interpret this physical act as a symbolic purification of the soul, where the creature represents the ego or excessive attachment (*'ishq*) that must be shed to achieve spiritual balance. The initial turning away signifies the need for introspection, while the subsequent relief indicates the successful removal of the burden of worldly attachment.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Umar Bin Ali Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Umar, from his brother Al Husayn, from his father Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and in his<sup>asws</sup> presence was a man who said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I love the children’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘So what is it that you do?’ He said, ‘I carry them upon my back’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> placed his<sup>asws</sup> hand upon his forehead and turned his<sup>asws</sup> face away from him. So the man wept, and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> looked at him as if he<sup>asws</sup> pitied him, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you go to your city, so buy a fat camel and tie it with an intense tying, and take the sword and strike the hump with a striking, taking off its skin, and sit upon it with its heat’.

So Umar (the narrator) said, ‘So the man said (afterwards), ‘I went to my city and bought a camel, and I tied it down with an intense tying, and took the sword, so I struck the hump with it with a strike, and then took the skin off it, and I sat upon it with its heat. So there dropped from me, upon the back of the camel, something resembling the lizard, being smaller than the lizard, and what was with me settled down’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Musa ibn al-Hassan from ‘Umar ibn Ali ibn ‘Amr ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn ‘Umar from his brother al-Husayn from his father ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following:

“Once, when, I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a man also was there. He said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I love children.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Why is it?’ He said, ‘I carry them on my back.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, placed his hand on his forehead and turned his face away from him. The man cried and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, looked to him as if he sympathized and said, ‘When you go to your town buy a healthy camel and tie it down firmly then take a sword and slash its hump to take away its skin and sit on it as it is naturally hot.’

‘Umar has said that the man said, ‘When I returned to my town I bought a healthy camel, tied it down firmly, took the sword and took away its skin and sat on it as it was naturally warm and on the back of the camel from me fell something like a small frog (lizard) and my problem calmed down.’”
